nuclearnicer 2026/08/11 20:27
这是一个精明的观点。我同意我们在很大程度上失去了很多共同的现实。但就像一个漫长而分散的过程的任何“开始”一样，人们可能会对具体细节争论不休。

我提供了一些你可能会认为是共享现实终结的开始的其他时刻。

首先是 1987 年，随着公平主义的废除以及随后党派谈话广播节目的繁荣。

第二个是 1989 年，当时有线电视成为一项成熟的技术，覆盖了美国一半的人口。最后，也许是一个较小的项目，大约 2000 年 DVR 的引入，当时我们不再一起观看预定的电视节目。

我想知道，随着出版技术的其他进步允许更多的人分享更多的观点，更多了解历史的人是否会发现更早的破裂。

It is an astute point. I agree that we have largely lost a lot of our shared reality. But as with any "beginning" of a long, diffuse process, people might quibble about the specifics.

I offer a few other moments you might gesture toward as the beginning of the end of shared reality.

First, 1987, with the elimination of the Fairness Doctrine and the subsequent boom in partisan talk radio shows.

Second, 1989, when cable TV became a mature technology reaching half of U.S. households.

And finally, maybe a lesser item, the introduction of the DVR circa 2000, when we stopped watching scheduled TV together.

I wonder if more historically informed people would find the fracturing going further back as other advancements in publishing technology allowed more people to share more views.

hnlmorg 2026/08/11 21:18
什么是“共享现实”？例如，我和我妈妈可以在电影院观看完全相同的电影和放映，但仍然对它有完全不同的看法。

即使电视仅限于少数几个全国性 OTA（无线）频道，不同的人也会在不同的时间收看他们不同的节目偏好。因此，仅仅因为内容较少，并不一定意味着不同的人消费相同的内容。

现代问题的真正症结不是偏好驱动选择。独立出版商被企业的贪婪驱逐。例如，人工智能流量使得独立博客变得不可行。但人们可能会说，当前的生态系统（出版门槛如此之低）是一种反常现象，因为从历史上看，出版成本总是高得令人望而却步。回到电视的例子：如果没有雄厚的资金和大量的电视高管联系人，你就无法委托制作一档节目。

我希望我们的信息黄金时代能够持续下去。但是，正如您和其他人所提到的，除非我们努力保持这种状态，否则这并不能得到保证。

What even is a “shared reality”? For example my mum and I could watch the exact same movie and showing at the cinema and still come away with a completely different opinion of it.

And even when TV was limited to a small few national OTA (over the air) channels, different people would tune in at different times to watch their different preference of shows. So just because content was fewer, it didn’t necessarily equate to different people consuming the same content.

The real crux of the modern problem isn’t preference drive choices. It’s independent publishers being driven out by corporate greed. Eg AI traffic making it unviable for independent blogs. But then one could argue that the current ecosystem, where the barrier for publishing being so low, is an anomaly because historically that was always prohibitively expensive. To go back to the TV example: you couldn’t commission a show without deep pockets and a lot of TV exec contacts.

I’d love our golden age of information to be persistent. But, and as yourself and others have alluded to, that’s not guaranteed unless we fight to keep it that way.

>什么是“共享现实”？例如，我和我妈妈可能在电影院观看完全相同的电影并放映，但仍然对它有完全不同的看法。

完全正确。共同的现实就是体验。你们都有相同的机会接受相同的信息。不同的观点来自于处理体验的肉套装的另一面。

Exactly. The shared reality is the experience. You both were given the same opportunity to take in the same information. The different opinion is what comes out of the other side of the meat suit processing the experience.

Algo driven results changes the experience by changing what the user perceives. So there might never be a shared experience.
